pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented via screen share as full form tutorials for every kettlebell exercise, double-bell and mace work, two three-month programmes, Trevor's own monthly challenge and full mobility and travel routines. The prospect volunteered that this was the core value for him: 'that seems pretty interesting to get the kind of the layout of all the exercises and going through them. I think that would be one of the most valuable things.' He then asked whether it was mobile-optimised mid-workout, a buying-style question.

Rep positioned it as whole-food and micronutrient focused rather than carnivore: 'It's not carnivore per se, but we are focused on whole foods... staying away from all the grains'. Prospect had already been told he was 'kind of in alignment with our nutrition' and raised no questions or pushback.

Presented as the Thursday 30-minute group class plus 30-minute Q&A and the Skool community — 'load them up through the week and hammer Trevor with them on the group class'. Prospect responded positively but only about the community layer: 'the community aspect is cool.' He did not tie it to his own goal and asked no mechanics questions.

anchors.raw: The coaching for three months would be 4K US, and the self-guided is just 200 bucks a month.
anchors.note: The rep introduced the $200/month self-guided product in the same breath as the coaching price, before any commitment check. That number became the prospect's anchor within seconds and he never returned to the coaching: '200 a month seems pretty legit, and it seems like there's a lot of stuff there'. The strongest price anchor on this call was created by Primal itself.

anchors.raw: I'm checking out a couple other programs, and you're like the second one I've looked at here and trying to see what really fits.
anchors.note: Prospect is running an active comparison against four options ('once I do all four of them, I'll make a decision') and named none of them. The rep never asked who the others were or what they cost, so the corpus loses the competitive intelligence and the rep lost any chance to differentiate.

anchors.raw: I'm still smashing my wrists on my cleans and kind of watching a lot of videos for that stuff
anchors.competitor: Free online video content, including Trevor's own social media
anchors.note: The prospect's current solution is free video, including Primal's own organic content, and it is the reason he is on the call at all: 'I see Trevor's stuff online... he's one of the dudes that I go to'. Free content is both the lead source and the price anchor.

anchors.raw: I probably melted 30 pounds off in the past year and a half, which is pretty good
anchors.note: He is already achieving the fat-loss outcome unaided, which structurally weakens the consequence case. The rep never tested this and never reframed the plateau, so the prospect's own track record stood as evidence that he does not need paid coaching.

unmet_demand.want: Form critique and technique correction on a mixed modality set — macebells, sandbags, rings and pull-up bar work alongside kettlebells — rather than a kettlebell-only programme
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep confirmed the programme combines kettlebells and calisthenics and showed mace tutorials, but never confirmed that sandbag, ring or macebell programming would be built into a tailored plan. The prospect asked directly and did not get a straight answer: 'is all that kind of incorporated with the calisthenics and stuff in the stuff that's done every week... I am looking for something a little more catered to me with the things I'm doing.'

unmet_demand.want: Short-duration, critique-only coaching — a few weeks of technique review and flow structuring, explicitly not long-term hand-holding
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The sanctioned offer is a 6- or 12-month coaching relationship. To serve this the rep improvised 3-month, 6-month and 1-month tiers live on the call. The prospect's need is real and recurring, but nothing in the approved product line matches it.

unmet_demand.want: A defined progression rule — how to know when he has earned the next bell weight and what to do after hitting a benchmark
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Explicitly asked ('for like four weeks here, and if I hit this benchmark, how do I progress? Or do I stay with the same stuff?') and never answered. The coaching almost certainly delivers exactly this and the rep did not say so; he moved on to the price ladder instead.
